findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext records logs on an unreachable logger
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware now logs every request through m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...). The new TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger(), i.e. a different TestLogger instance with its own empty Logs. The log call therefore goes to an instance the test cannot access, while the TestLogger passed to NewLoggerMiddleware remains with InfoLogs.Calls == 0. Existing logger-middleware tests that inspect the supplied TestLogger will fail, and the new contextual logging behavior cannot be asserted. The fake should return the receiver or a logger sharing the same Logs sink.

findings.title: No test covers the moved contextual logging and middleware ordering
findings.body: The PR moves pluginId, endpoint, user, data source, and trace attributes out of the metrics/logger middleware and makes LoggerMiddleware depend on the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware plus Logger.FromContext. The only test touched, metrics_middleware_test.go, still asserts metrics only; no test verifies the new middleware or the two-middleware interaction. A wrong middleware ordering or a FromContext implementation that drops the attributes would silently remove all request identifiers from backend plugin logs without failing tests. Add a test that chains ContextualLoggerMiddleware before LoggerMiddleware and asserts the logged InfoLogs contain endpoint, pluginId, dsName/dsUID, uname, and traceID.
